decisions.reason: The existing Event captures ticket visibility and backfill but omits the explicit one-to-one consistency rule between issued tickets and $5 commissions.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
At this point, we have completed 12 mints, so that should amount to 12 tickets & 12 x $5 commissions.

**Even if no referral code is used, a ticket and commission are still issued**.

Currently, **when a code is used**, it is accurately reflected on the leaderboards/NFT attributes. Perfect.

If **no referral code is used**, the ticket and commission are assigned at random.
(B**ut they must still be reflected on the leaderboard/NFT attributes**.)

I believe that since your most recent fix, the randomly assigned tickets from the last 2 mints have been reflected on the leaderboard/NFT attributes. Great.
However, the missing tickets have not been backfilled.

The commissions from these purchases without a code are also still not reflected on the leaderboard/NFT attributes.

In my screenshot, you will see that I have an NFT showing 2 tickets but only 1 x $5 commission. That should not be possible because each ticket includes a $5 commission.

Also, in my leaderboard screenshot, only 7 tickets and 5 x $5 commissions are accounted for out of 12 total mints.
Whether or not a referral code is used, 12 mints should result in 12 tickets and 12 x $5 commissions.

value_updates.ticket_surface_consistency_rule: Tickets awarded through both code-used and no-code mints must be reflected on leaderboards and NFT attributes.
value_updates.ticket_commission_consistency_rule: Every issued ticket must correspond to one $5 commission, so ticket and commission counts must remain consistent across aggregate and per-NFT views.

decisions.reason: The existing Event requires reward attributes and historical backfill but omits the explicit requirement that each NFT's ticket and $5 commission counts remain paired.

decisions.reason: The existing same-message Event already records one $5 commission for every primary mint, while random recipient selection was established earlier and remains unchanged.
The message clarifies accounting behavior during debugging but does not request a change to FAQ copy.
The existing same-message Event records one ticket per no-referral mint; its random-recipient and registration rules were already established.
Random allocation of no-referral tickets does not change the VRF draw method or eligibility rule; holders of such eligible tickets were already covered by the existing population definition.
The source confirms that code-used commissions are already represented correctly and does not change their amount, trigger, recipient, destination, or timing.
The accounting clarification does not instruct that the About page or its rendered process copy be revised.
Whether a code is used affects reward allocation and accounting, not the identity, lifetime, sharing, display, or resale behavior of an NFT's referral code.
The source establishes that the $5 commission allocation applies to every completed primary mint, not only code-used mints, making the prior code-limited revenue attribute stale.
